facts.text: Rail and aviation safety and simulation standards belong to industries that have accepted simulation as evidence for longer than road or off-road vehicle industries have.
facts.quote: These are the safety and simulation standards of two industries, railways and aviation, that have accepted simulation as evidence for longer than road or off-road vehicles have.

facts.text: EN 50126, EN 50128 and EN 50129 are European railway standards covering reliability and safety management, software and electronic signaling.
facts.quote: EN 50126, EN 50128 and EN 50129 are the European railway standards for reliability and safety management, software and electronic signaling

facts.text: EN 50716:2023 is the current railway software standard and the successor to EN 50128.
facts.quote: EN 50716:2023 is the current railway software standard and successor to EN 50128.

facts.text: The booklet lists EN 50126, EN 50128, EN 50129 and EN 50716 as not verified.
facts.quote: The booklet lists all four as not verified [Chapter 10].

facts.text: EN 14363:2016+A2:2022 is the standard for accepting railway vehicle running behavior; Annex T covers simulation of on-track tests, and Annex U covers extension of acceptance to vehicles of the same basic design.
facts.quote: EN 14363:2016+A2:2022, the standard for accepting the running behavior of railway vehicles, was studied closely: its Annex T covers simulation of on-track tests and Annex U extension of acceptance to vehicles of the same basic design.

facts.text: Railway validation practice related to EN 14363 uses at least 24 simulation-versus-measurement comparisons drawn from at least 12 track sections.
facts.quote: In the related practice, at least 24 simulation-versus-measurement comparisons are drawn from at least 12 track sections

facts.text: Railway validation practice related to EN 14363 sets validation limits on the whole set of simulation-versus-measurement deviations.
facts.quote: validation limits are set on the whole set of deviations

facts.text: European Union Agency for Railways guidance describes modifying a validated model to represent a changed vehicle and using the modified model as evidence.
facts.quote: the European Union Agency for Railways' guidance describes modifying a validated model to represent a changed vehicle and using it as evidence

facts.text: DynoTRAIN research behind the railway validation method compared many models and tools against measurements.
facts.quote: the DynoTRAIN research behind the method compared many models and tools against measurements [Chapter 10].

facts.text: DO-178C is the software standard for airborne systems, and DO-330 is its companion for qualifying software tools whose output is relied on without further checking.
facts.quote: DO-178C is the software standard for airborne systems and DO-330 its companion on qualifying software tools whose output is relied on without further checking

facts.text: DO-330 does not address whether a physics model is valid.
facts.quote: DO-330 "does not address whether a physics model is valid"

facts.text: The booklet lists DO-178C and DO-330 as not verified.
facts.quote: both are listed as not verified [Chapter 10].

facts.text: DO-385 and its European twin ED-256 are the minimum operational performance standards for Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X), the new aircraft collision-avoidance system.
facts.quote: DO-385 and its European twin ED-256 are the minimum operational performance standards for the Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X), the new aircraft collision-avoidance system

entities.name: Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X)

facts.text: Aviation standards bodies RTCA and EUROCAE published DO-385 and ED-256 in October 2018.
facts.quote: published in October 2018 by the aviation standards bodies RTCA and EUROCAE

facts.text: ACAS X was validated largely by simulating encounters equivalent to billions of flight hours.
facts.quote: the system was validated largely by simulating encounters equivalent to billions of flight hours [Chapter 2].

entities.name: Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X)

facts.text: Railway practice provides the booklet's clearest model of validation-domain extension by similarity plus bridging evidence: validate a family model at the corners of its envelope, document differences when a vehicle changes, and conduct targeted extra tests. The booklet identifies this argument as the shape needed to cover many heavy off-road machine models and sensor positions.
facts.quote: a family model validated at the corners of the envelope, with a documented difference and targeted extra tests when a vehicle changes, which is the shape of argument needed to cover many machine models and sensor positions [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Aviation provides the booklet with the tool-qualification idea and a precedent for statistical simulation accepted by standards bodies and authorities after years of developing the underlying models.
facts.quote: Aviation gives the tool-qualification idea and a precedent of statistical simulation accepted by standards bodies and authorities after years of building the underlying models [Chapters 2, 10].
